case_name: Smt. Sunita v. Shri Rajesh Kumar — full case name

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: wife, mother of two minor children
parties.respondent_defendant: husband, father of two minor children

acts_cited_auto: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

acts_cited.act: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

facts_of_case: The parties were married in 2005. The respondent used to beat the petitioner and also used to abuse her verbally. The petitioner filed a complaint under Section 12 of the Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005. The trial court allowed the petition and granted protection order to the petitioner.

legal_principles.principle: The burden lies on the respondent to prove that the allegations of domestic violence are false.
legal_principles.held: It is held that the burden lies on the respondent to prove that the allegations of domestic violence are false. The court cannot take a mechanical approach and require the complainant to prove every detail of the incident.
applicable_acts_sections: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005 — Section 10

legal_principles.principle: The court must consider the entire evidence on record and not just rely on the complainant's testimony.
legal_principles.held: This court holds that the court must consider the entire evidence on record and not just rely on the complainant's testimony. The court cannot ignore the evidence of other witnesses who may have corroborated the complainant's version.

outcome.final_order: The final court order confirmed the protection order granted by the trial court in favor of the petitioner.
